title: Pork and Watercress with Soy-Based Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Pork and watercress with soy-based sauce is a dish that combines tender pork, the peppery bite of watercress, and a savory soy sauce made from fermented soybeans. It is popular in Asian cuisine and is usually served hot as a main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Watercress is rich in vitamin C, potassium, and glucosinolates, which have antioxidant properties.
The soy sauce used is traditionally fermented for several months, giving it a deep umami flavor.
Pork provides high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins, and zinc.
The dish is often paired with rice or noodles, creating a balanced carbohydrate‑protein meal.
In traditional Chinese cooking, watercress is sometimes substituted with spinach or bok choy.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork supplies complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Watercress adds vitamin C, vitamin K, and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Soy sauce contains enzymes and polyphenols that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Watercress provides dietary fiber, promoting regular bowel movements.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The combination of protein and moderate fat makes the dish a good source of sustained energy.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy sauce.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is salty; people with hypertension should limit their portion.

items.title: Proper pork cooking
items.content: Pork must be cooked thoroughly to avoid salmonella or trichinella risks.

items.title: Watercress safety
items.content: Watercress can harbor bacteria; use fresh, well‑washed leaves.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically over steamed rice, noodles, or alongside vegetable sides. A squeeze of fresh lemon or a dash of chili can enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Fresh watercress is best used immediately; any remaining leaves should be stored dry, wrapped in a damp paper towel.
